title: Contract Phasing Fractionation Heatmap Simulation - June 2030
summary: Simulation sheet to fractionate committed GPU slabs across regions and contracts, produce a heatmap of utilization under 3 demand trajectories, and propose reallocation triggers and burst policies.
content:
OVERVIEW:
This sheet simulates contract-level phasing and fractionation for dedicated GPU reservations across four regions (us-west, us-east, europe-west, apac-sg). Purpose: identify vulnerable contracts (under/over-utilized), surface where fractionation (splitting slabs across regions or time windows) reduces unmet demand, and quantify expected unit-hours savings under three demand trajectories.

ASSUMPTIONS:
- Time horizon: 12 months (Jul 2029 - Jun 2030) phased monthly.
- Unit: vGPU-equivalent (1 vGPU = 1 A100-80GB equivalent).
- Committed slabs are reserved 24/7 unless explicitly scheduled as 'phased' (time-blocked).
- Burst pool: shared global pool of on-demand GPUs used when committed slabs are saturated; cost preference is to minimize burst usage subject to latency SLOs.
- Migration cost: moving a slab regionally incurs a 48-hour provisioning delay and a one-time reconfigure cost (captured as 0.5% of monthly committed spend in downstream finance model).
- Customer SLAs: priority tiers (P1, P2, P3) determine tolerance for phased reductions. P1 cannot be fractionated without exec approval.

INPUT TABLE (per-contract snapshots):
Columns: CONTRACT_ID | CUSTOMER | TIER | REGION_PRIMARY | COMMITTED_VGPU | PHASE_WINDOW (months) | AVG_UTIL_% (last 90d) | PEAK_95%_HOUR | MONTHLY_TOKEN_RUNRATE_EST | NOTES
Rows (examples):
C-3227 | HexaMaps | P2 | us-west | 96 | 0 | 42 | 160 | 1.1B | spikes localized eow compute
C-4190 | ClearVoice | P1 | us-east | 384 | 0 | 89 | 382 | 4.7B | latency-sensitive inference, no fractionation allowed
C-5501 | NimbusHealth | P3 | europe-west | 48 | 3 | 18 | 44 | 0.28B | can tolerate 40% phasing in Q4
C-6012 | RetailOps | P2 | apac-sg | 128 | 1 | 66 | 210 | 2.0B | heavy batch nightly, candidate for time-window phasing

REGIONAL INVENTORY SUMMARY (current reserved pool):
us-west: 2,560 vGPU committed (60% utilization baseline)
us-east: 3,840 vGPU committed (74% utilization baseline)
europe-west: 1,120 vGPU committed (38% utilization baseline)
apac-sg: 960 vGPU committed (52% utilization baseline)
Global burst pool (on-demand): 1,200 vGPU-equivalent

SCENARIOS MODELED:
- Conservative (baseline demand growth +2% monthly)
- Medium (baseline +6% monthly + 15% seasonality in Nov-Feb)
- Aggressive (baseline +12% monthly + 30% seasonality)
For each scenario we re-run per-contract monthly utilization projection and compute expected unmet-hours that would hit the burst pool.

SIMULATION OUTPUT (high level):
- Conservative: projected global utilization avg 63%, monthly burst usage negligible (<= 3% of burst pool). 7 contracts flagged for potential fractionation to smooth regional hotspots (mostly apac/us-west).
- Medium: projected avg 74%, burst pool usage median 22% (peak 47%), 18 contracts flagged, recommended partial phasing or cross-region fractionation for 9 contracts with flexible SLAs.
- Aggressive: projected avg 91%, burst pool exhausted in 40% of months, 34 contracts flagged, urgent negotiation recommended for 6 P1 contracts to expand dedicated capacity or accept fallbacks.

FRACTIONATION HEATMAP (conceptual, extract shown as bucket counts):
- Heatmap axis: Contracts (rows) x Months (cols), cell = fractionation % recommended (0 = leave monolithic).
- Example summary: 12 contracts recommended to be split 50/50 across two regions during peak months; 5 contracts recommended to be time-blocked (night-only for 30% of capacity).

RECOMMENDED ACTIONS (per-contract):
- C-3227 (HexaMaps): split 96 -> 48 us-west / 48 us-east during Nov-Feb; expected burst reduction 18% in us-west peaks. Phase window: Nov-Feb (3 months). Impact to customer SLA: negligible (P2).
- C-4190 (ClearVoice): no fractionation; urgent add-on proposal for +128 vGPU in us-east to meet aggressive scenario. Finance motion: prepare addendum for Q3 commit.
- C-5501 (NimbusHealth): convert 48 committed to 30/18 time-blocked (night batch) for months Jul-Sep to cover other customers; requires signed amended schedule with 30% discount.

RE-ALLOCATION RULES / TRIGGERS:
- Soft trigger: regional utilization > 80% for 7 consecutive days -> recommend notify customer & propose fractionation.
- Hard trigger: regional utilization > 90% for 72 hours OR burst usage > 70% for 7 days -> automatic temporary regional reassign of flexible P3/P2 slabs (subject to customer opt-out) and engage capacity on-call.
- Migration throttle: limit to 3 concurrent contract moves per region-week to avoid capacity thrash.

COST & FINANCIAL SENSITIVITY (simplified):
- Fractionation saves on average 4-9% of monthly committed spend by reducing necessary burst pool top-ups; larger for highly seasonal customers.
- Migration overhead modeled as 0.5% monthly committed spend per move; breakeven typically within 4-6 months for contracts with >25% peak mismatches.

OPERATIONAL PLAYBOOK (steps for on-call & capacity ops):
1) Run nightly simulation and append heatmap changes to the 'phasing queue' (priority sorted by expected burst reduction).
2) Auto-open advisory ticket for contracts crossing soft trigger, assign to Solutions Eng.
3) For hard triggers, enact emergency reassign and notify CS/Account Execs; log migration in allocation ledger.
4) Post-migration: run 14-day stability window before further changes.

DECISION LOG (open questions):
- How to price multi-region fractionation for enterprise customers (one-time vs recurring discount)? Action: finance + commercial to propose 2 models by Jul 15.
- Acceptable migration throttle policy for P1 customers under aggressive scenarios? Action: legal + customer success to draft amendment.

NEXT STEPS / OWNER ACTIONS:
- Priya Shah: validate contract opt-out clauses for fractionation by 2029-06-25.
- Liam O'Connor: build automated nightly simulation job with delta alerting by 2029-07-05.
- Marcus Nguyen (owner): schedule cross-functional review (Finance/CS/Platform) 2029-06-21.

APPENDIX (calculation notes):
- Utilization projection = last-90d avg * (1 + monthly-growth)^months.
- Burst need per month = max(0, projected_peak_hours - available_committed_hours) aggregated across regions.
- Fractionation recommended when projected burst-hours reduction > 8% of regional burst capacity AND migration breakeven <= 6 months.

RAW CSV EXPORT (how sheet will be exported):
contract_id,customer,tier,primary_region,committed_vgpu,phased_months,avg_util_pct,proj_peak_hour,proj_burst_hours,recommended_action,est_burst_reduction_pct,notes
C-3227,HexaMaps,P2,us-west,96,3,42,160,120,split-50-50,18,seasonal eow spikes
C-4190,ClearVoice,P1,us-east,384,0,89,382,900,expand-commit,0,latency-sensitive
C-5501,NimbusHealth,P3,europe-west,48,3,18,44,0,time-block-night-30,6,good candidate for backfill

This sheet is an operational sim – treat numbers as inputs to decisions, not hard SLAs. Keep updated model parameters in linked Confluence page (confluence:INFRA-CAPACITY-2030).
